rationale: Wrong-book misattribution. The node is explicitly about Eusebius PE VI.6.22-73 (the Origenist theodicy following the Carneadean arguments, with the Republic hierophant axiom αἰτία ἑλομένου θεὸς ἀναίτιος). The current citation is to PE book 5 (passage bdd5c7a4: 'the Greeks confessing their oracles ceased after the saviour's teaching') — a book-5 topic on oracles, off-theme for the book-6 anti-fatalism theodicy. The exact VI.6.22-73 text with the αἰτία ἑλομένου axiom is NOT in the corpus (all αἰτία ἑλομένου hits are Plato Rep. 617 and Justin, not Eusebius). The verified best in-corpus target is the PE book-6 proem (passage e311f0e8, urn ...:6), which opens precisely the book on fate/free will: 'τῆς θείας δυνάμεως τοῦ σωτῆρος... ἐπιδεδει[γμένης]' after the oracles are refuted. Repointing PE5→PE6 corrects the book and lands the citation inside the correct book the node describes. Conservative: targets the book-6 proem, not the exact 22-73 sub-section (which the partial corpus does not hold); the existing confidence is already 0.75. A future pass should narrow to VI.6 once that sub-section is ingested.

The claim is the Carneadean anti-fatalist chain (assent/tendency/action all effects of antecedent causes => not in our power => praise/blame unjust => probably not all by fate). The cited Fat. 17 passage (47636aac...) is about DIODORUS's modal thesis ('only what is or will be true is possible; future truths as immutable as past') — Diodorus material, not the Carneadean moral assent-chain. The correct support is Cicero De Fato 31, which is in the corpus (passage 7bdfd343-..., canonical_ref 'Fat. 31'): Carneades's argument that 'if all things happen by antecedent causes in natural connection, necessity produces all; but something is in our power; therefore not all happens by fate' — directly the chain premise. Repointed Fat. 17 -> Fat. 31. (Note: the node's prose 'De fato 17, 40' references Amand's reconstruction and is left untouched; only the citation edge is corrected.)

De Fato 24 argues the distinct regress-of-causes / 'nothing comes to be uncaused' reply (ἀναιτίως... τῶν αἰτίων), not the 'for the most part' (ὡς ἐπὶ τὸ πλεῖστον) nature argument this node describes. The argument's distinctive vocabulary (ὡς ἐπὶ τὸ πλεῖστον, παρὰ φύσιν, ἀμείνων τῆς φύσεως, the Socrates example) is absent from this passage, and corpus search finds no occurrence of ὡς ἐπὶ τὸ πλεῖστον in any De Fato section. Cited as source_for at confidence 1.0 but does not support the claim; no verified better corpus target, so remove rather than repoint.

Citation Strom. II.11.50 concerns the gnostic abstaining from sins of word/thought/sense and the symbolism of the three measures ('ὁ τοίνυν γνωστικὸς ἀφέξεται... ἁμαρτημάτων'). It does not contain the Carneadean faith/unbelief-punishment argument the node quotes (located at Strom. II.11.1-2 ≈48-49, not present in the corpus). Unsupporting for this specific argument; no valid in-corpus repoint target. Remove.

Description (per Amand) targets the anti-Marcionite/Demiurge excursus at Phil. 23.2 (Robinson p.188,30–189,18): the Demiurge denied justice, the astral-slavery aporia. The single cited passage is Philocalia 23.3, whose text is about divine prescience and 'que les luminaires servent de signes' (eyewitness vs. hearsay knowledge) — a different argument within Phil. 23. Corpus search for the described content (Marcionites, Démiurge, esclaves de la nécessité, génération astrale) returns found:false, so no verified repoint target exists. Node already carries needs_evidence:true; remove the non-supporting citation rather than invent a target.

Citation Strom. II.11.52 concerns Abraham standing before the Lord, Simon Magus 'the Standing One', and faith/gnosis vs. apostasy ('ἡ πίστις οὖν ἥ τε γνῶσις τῆς ἀληθείας... κατασκευάζουσι τὴν ἑλομένην αὐτὰς ψυχήν'). While it touches faith and the choosing soul, it does NOT contain the specific Carneadean faith/unbelief-punishment argument the node quotes (Strom. II.11.1-2 / ≈48-49), which is not in the corpus. Thematically adjacent but does not support the quoted claim; no valid in-corpus repoint target for this specific argument. Remove.

Node claims the Carneadean faith/unbelief responsibility argument of Strom. II.11.1-2 ('if faith is a prerogative of nature... he who does not believe will not be justly punished'). But this citation is Strom. II.11.51, whose text concerns ascent to the nous and the symbolism of the decade/Passover ('τὰς ἐννέα μοίρας ὑπερπηδήσαντας... ἐπὶ τὴν γνῶσιν... τοῦ θεοῦ'). It does not contain the quoted faith/unbelief-punishment argument, which falls at the START of Strom. II.11 (≈II.11.48-49 GCS) — a section absent from the corpus (verified: only II.11.50-52 are held; the term νενευροσπαστημένων returns found:false). The claim and Amand 1945 reference are genuine scholarship, but this passage does not support them and no in-corpus passage carries the argument. Remove.
